item.description:
## Added

- CLI Proxy API accounts now work end to end. The setup assistant's first page
  recognises them as a sign-in, the Transcription step lets you pick the
  sign-in source and account without leaving setup, and a new Account
  directory setting points Speecher at a custom CLI Proxy API folder when the
  automatic detection doesn't find yours.
- The setup assistant was rebuilt around honest checks on every platform: each
  step verifies what it set up, holds Next until it actually works, and the
  final page lists exactly what is left when something isn't.
- An opt-in accuracy pass for ChatGPT Codex dictation retranscribes the whole
  recording when you stop, catching mistakes the live stream made. Off by
  default; find it on the Transcription step or the Audio settings.
- Dictation now applies hesitation self-corrections: "meet at five — no, six"
  delivers six.
- Push-to-talk on Linux: hold your Global Shortcut to dictate, release to
  stop, on desktops whose portal reports key release (Plasma and GNOME 48+).
- Speecher lives in the Linux system tray with quick access to dictation and
  settings.
- Transcription and refinement previews have separate toggles, so you can
  watch the raw words land but skip the cleanup shimmer, or the other way
  around.
- Sign-ins from the native Codex app now work, alongside the Codex CLI.

## Changed

- Setting a shortcut is one control now: click, press your combination or
  single key, done. No more edit-then-apply, and single keys work everywhere
  combinations do.
- The Linux dictation popup is drawn in your desktop's own style, with the
  waveform pill matching the transcript pill.
- The sidebar draws its splitter as a translucent hairline and keeps your
  selection highlighted while the window is unfocused.

## Fixed

- Dictations no longer lose text when a speech stream drops or delivery races
  a restart; interrupted sessions carry their words through.
- Dictated lists keep the numbers you spoke instead of renumbering from 1.
- Windows: dictation no longer trips a 429 at start, and the preview sizes to
  match macOS and Linux.
- macOS: the dictation preview no longer drifts left, and Claude sign-in reads
  the Keychain reliably.
- Linux: setup works without a polkit agent, the key-watch helper installs
  cleanly, terminal paste reaches GPU terminals that aren't on the
  accessibility bus, and a missing AT-SPI peer no longer crashes dictation.
- Adding a key term works again: the Add button on Linux, term-less records on
  macOS.
- Nightly updates download the exact build the update offer was signed for, so
  an accepted offer can't be rejected after a newer nightly lands.
